:::{#exm-second-derivative}
#### The second derivative of $x^3$

For $f(x) = x^3$, the power rule (@thm-deriv-polynomial) gives $f'(x) = 3x^2$ at every $x$,
and differentiating again, with the constant multiple rule (@thm-deriv-const-factor), gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
f''(x) &= 3 \cd 2x \\
&= 6x.
\end{aligned}
$$

So $f''(2) = 12$, $f''(0) = 0$, and $f''(-1) = -6$.

:::
